stories.headline: Juniper Ridge starts its 5A title defense without seven regulars
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Bryce Seaver lost one match last season. He went 35-1, mostly at No. 2 doubles, and he graduated in June with six other Juniper Ridge regulars, Rafael Rivera at first singles and Ricardo Rodriguez (33-3) among them.
That is the roster coach Ray Okafor takes to Liberty Hill Monday to begin defending the 5A championship Juniper Ridge won in October, after an 18-0 run through the Kajaani League.

Three players who won 28 matches apiece are back. Seniors Ezekiel Amoore and Deon Rennick and junior Joshua Butcher spent most of their time in doubles, and all three took turns at the top of the singles order during Saturday's last practice before the opener. Okafor reshuffled it after every rotation.
"I don't have a one yet and I'm not pretending I do," Okafor said. "Zeke, Deon and Josh all think it's them. Levi probably thinks it's him too, and he's the only one who never lost."
Levi is Levi Chesnut, a sophomore who went 16-0 as a freshman playing second and third singles. Four freshmen are also on the roster, including Dimitri Kimball.
Juniper Ridge plays four duals in four days: at Liberty Hill, then home against Pacersburg and Westfield Friends of Fort Meriwether, then the Kajaani League opener Thursday at Cedar Exchange.

stories.headline: Carroway sorts seven freshmen before Wednesday's opener
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: "Seven freshmen and a final to get back to," Carroway coach Linda Haverkamp said, counting the names on her clipboard twice. "I keep getting the same number."

Carroway lost the 3A state final in October. Its two players at first singles, Asher Barrett and Bronson Koontz, have graduated, and Haverkamp said the freshmen, Uwe Fiebich and Rashad McCloud among them, will play their way into doubles spots in the opening week.

Senior Luke Palm (23-4) and junior James Stacy (20-5) played almost all of their matches in doubles. Junior Jasper Kuroda went 14-4, mostly at second singles, and senior Max Callender went 9-3 at third.
Carroway opens Wednesday at home against Pacersburg. The Juniper League opener is Aug. 8 at Ostrander Union, which finished second in the standings.

stories.headline: County by county: the Desert Sky race and a crosstown opener
body: RIMROCK COUNTY

Vesper and Silton Ridge. The two finished first and second in the 1A Desert Sky League, Silton Ridge at 14-2 and Vesper at 12-4, and both reached the state quarterfinals. Vesper keeps sophomore Taras Piątek, who won 26 of 29 matches as a freshman, almost all at No. 1 and No. 2 doubles. Silton Ridge has nine seniors and a junior, William Lemke, who went 21-5 in doubles. The two do not meet in the opening two weeks.
Covenant. The Premier Athletic Association champion (11-1) plays three of its first five duals on the road, two of them in league play.

Dry Lake. Second in the Fiesta Athletic Association, and the four players who carried it are juniors Lawrence Sullivan and Lorenzo Morlan and sophomores Noah Sorenson and Teagan Combs. All four played 31 matches.
JUNIPER COUNTY

Altamonte and Senator Gray. The 8A schools across town from each other open the season against each other Monday at Senator Gray. Altamonte carries eight seniors. Senator Gray's Cranston Diggins (18-10) and John Jensen (20-8) both played first singles a year ago and are both seniors now.
California Canyons. Hudson Chiu, a junior, played first singles for the Dual County League champions and went 16-12.
Mt Jacqueline. Ryder Nale went 26-4 as a sophomore, mostly at No. 3 doubles.
High Desert Christian. Did not win a Juniper League dual in 16 tries. Its four busiest players from that team are seniors.

stories.headline: 12 area duals open the season Monday
body: All 12 are invitationals. Silton Ridge travels to Espoo, a 1A state semifinalist a year ago. Central West End is at Calder, California Canyons at Summervale and Trout Lake at Star Hollow.
